claims.text: The starting WTaVTi precursor is nominally equiatomic.
The precursor has a dendrite–interdendrite structure consisting of approximately 71 vol.% connected W/Ta-rich dendrites and 29 vol.% Ti/V-rich channels.
Immersion of the WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h causes liquid-metal dealloying.
The dealloying treatment preferentially dissolves Ti from the interdendritic channels.
The treatment produces a directionally aligned bicontinuous composite containing approximately 63.6 vol.% BCC RHEA ligaments and 36.4 vol.% nearly pure FCC Cu channels.
A W-rich interlayer approximately 300 nm thick forms spontaneously at each RHEA/Cu interface.
Minor HCP Ti-rich precipitates are present in the dealloyed composite.
Ti has a negative heat of mixing with Cu.
Preferential Ti dissolution leaves W, Ta, and V behind to form the RHEA ligaments.
W has a strong positive heat of mixing with Cu.
Continued Ti extraction traps W at the RHEA/Cu interface and creates the passivating interlayer.
The W-rich interlayer arrests further interfacial exchange and promotes stable RHEA/Cu bonding.
The W-rich interlayer prevents or reduces interfacial void formation.
The aligned Cu channels provide effective heat-conduction pathways.
The proposed structure boosts high-temperature thermal conductivity through enhanced lattice-mediated transport.
The dealloyed composite will have substantially higher thermal conductivity above approximately 650 °C than the untreated WTaVTi precursor and conventional W–Cu composites.
Thermal-conductivity benefits are expected above 1000 °C based on extrapolation from measurements made only up to approximately 800 °C.
The dealloyed composite will exhibit less helium-induced swelling, blistering, or cracking than pure W under 25 keV He+ implantation near 8–8.5 × 10^17 atoms/cm².
The proposed thermal advantages are limited to directionally dealloyed material with the specified phase segregation and are expected primarily above approximately 650 °C.
The irradiation prediction applies only to low-energy 25 keV He+ screening and does not establish behavior under neutron irradiation or vacancy-driven swelling.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis refers to improvement relative to an 'untreated composite,' but the stated untreated starting material is a WTaVTi precursor containing no Cu, while conventional W–Cu composites are separate literature baselines. The identity of the primary untreated-composite control is therefore inconsistent.

The requested starting point is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or ligaments in Cu, whereas the proposed starting material is a Cu-free WTaVTi precursor; Cu is introduced only during dealloying. Thus, the intervention replaces rather than modifies the specified initial material system.
